questions.text: Why is Layer Normalization preferred over Batch Normalization in transformers?
options: Layer Norm uses fewer parameters
Layer Norm normalizes across features within a single sample, independent of batch size
Layer Norm is faster to compute
Layer Norm does not require any learnable parameters
questions.explanation: Layer Norm normalizes across the feature dimension per sample, making it independent of batch size. This is crucial for variable-length sequences and autoregressive generation where batch size can be 1.

questions.text: What are the learnable parameters in Layer Normalization?
options: Gamma (γ) for scaling and Beta (β) for shifting
Mean (μ) and variance (σ²)
Query, Key, and Value matrices
Learning rate and epsilon
questions.explanation: After normalizing to zero mean and unit variance, gamma and beta allow the network to learn the optimal scale and shift for each feature dimension.

questions.text: What is the difference between pre-norm and post-norm in transformers?
options: Pre-norm applies normalization after the sublayer
Post-norm applies normalization before the sublayer
Pre-norm: x + Sublayer(LayerNorm(x)); Post-norm: LayerNorm(x + Sublayer(x))
They are identical in practice
questions.explanation: Pre-norm normalizes before the sublayer (used in GPT-2 and most modern LLMs), while post-norm normalizes after (original transformer). Pre-norm provides more stable gradient flow.

questions.text: Which of the following are true about RMSNorm?Select all that apply
options: It requires computing both mean and variance
It only normalizes by the root mean square, skipping mean centering
It is slower than Layer Norm
It is used in LLaMA and other modern architectures
questions.explanation: RMSNorm simplifies Layer Norm by removing mean centering, only dividing by the RMS. It is computationally cheaper and used in LLaMA, Gemma, and other modern architectures.

questions.text: What does the epsilon (ε) value in Layer Norm prevent?
options: Division by zero when variance is very small
Overflow in the mean calculation
Negative values in the output
Gradients from becoming too large
questions.explanation: Epsilon is a small constant (typically 1e-5) added to the variance before taking the square root, preventing division by zero when features are nearly identical.
